description.summary: launch desktop applications inside virtual machines

protocol.description:
Lets a client (the shell's app launcher) start an installed application inside a virtual machine instead of on the host. The compositor boots the VM, runs the program in it and shows its windows as ordinary windows on this desktop, marked with a badge (see the compositor's `[vm]` configuration for how VMs are set up).
A client names the application by its desktop entry id, never by a command line: the compositor resolves the id against the desktop entries installed on the host and runs that entry's `Exec` in the guest. A client can therefore only start things the user has installed as applications, not run arbitrary commands.
The global is not advertised to clients that run inside a VM themselves (so a guest cannot start further VMs on the host) nor to clients connected through a sandbox (security-context) socket.
Each launch is a separate object that reports the VM's progress: `starting`, then `running`, then (for a persistent VM) `saving`, and finally `finished`; or just `failed` if the launch is refused. Events are only informational: the VM does not depend on the client afterwards, and destroying the object (or disconnecting) leaves it running.

interface.name: ironland_vm_launcher_v1
interface.description: The manager global. On binding it immediately sends `availability`.

enum.name: mode

description.summary: what kind of VM to start

enum.description: Both kinds boot a VM from the configured guest image and show the program's windows on the host.
enum.entry: The VM runs on a temporary snapshot of the image that is thrown away when the program exits. Every launch boots from scratch and any number of VMs can run at once.

entry.name: persistent
entry.summary: the app's disk and memory are kept

enum.entry: The application keeps its own disk and, when its program exits cleanly, its memory state: the next persistent launch of the same application resumes where it left off, with all its files, in about a second instead of a full boot. At most one persistent VM per application runs at a time.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager. Launch objects created from it stay valid.

request.name: launch

description.summary: start an application in a new VM

request.description: Starts the application with the given desktop entry id in a VM and returns an object reporting how that goes. The compositor replies with `starting` once the VM process has been started (the window only appears later, when the guest has booted and the program has opened it), or with `failed` if the launch is refused.

arg.name: entry
arg.summary: desktop entry id, with or without the .desktop suffix

event.name: availability
event.description: Sent when the manager is bound and again whenever it changes. `configured` is 1 when the compositor has a guest image configured and launches can be attempted, 0 when it has none (every launch would fail with `not_configured`). A client should only offer VM launching while this is 1.

interface.name: ironland_vm_launch_v1
interface.description: Reports the life of one launched VM. Created by `ironland_vm_launcher_v1.launch`. After `failed` or `finished` no further events are sent.

entry.name: unknown_entry
entry.summary: no installed application has that desktop entry id

entry.name: image_missing
entry.summary: the configured guest image does not exist

entry.name: too_many
entry.summary: the limit on concurrent VMs is reached

entry.name: already_running
entry.summary: a persistent VM for this application is already running

entry.name: no_command
entry.summary: the entry has no command to run

entry.name: state
entry.summary: the persistent VM's saved state could not be prepared

entry.name: other
entry.summary: the VM could not be started

entry.name: closed
entry.summary: the program exited and the VM was shut down

entry.name: saved
entry.summary: the program exited and a persistent VM's state was saved

entry.name: failed
entry.summary: the VM or its window forwarding died unexpectedly

entry.name: timed_out
entry.summary: no window appeared in time, or saving the state took too long

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stops receiving events for this launch. Does not stop the VM.

event.name: failed
event.description: The launch could not be started. `message` is a short human-readable explanation suitable for showing to the user. The object is inert afterwards and should be destroyed.

event.name: starting
event.description: The VM process is up and the guest is booting (or, for a persistent VM with saved state, being restored). `vm` is an identifier for this VM, unique for the lifetime of the compositor.

event.name: running
event.description: The guest is up and the program has connected to the desktop, so its window is (about to be) on screen.

event.name: saving

description.summary: a persistent VM's state is being saved

event.description: The program exited and the compositor is saving the persistent VM's disk and memory state, which can take a few seconds. The next persistent launch of the same application is refused with `already_running` until `finished` arrives.

event.name: finished
event.description: The VM has been shut down.
